rationale: C04 plausibly supplied the child’s report-acknowledgment template: both Eisenhower letters praise a recently submitted study, characterize it as valuable to government deliberations, indicate how it will be used by relevant officials or bodies, and close with gratitude to the recipient and associates. C21 has a similar report-appreciation sequence but is more elaborate and less proximate in voice. C14 parallels the use of an advisory commission in coordination with the Office of Defense Mobilization, but its main function is establishing and appointing a committee rather than acknowledging a completed report.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The expression of deep appreciation I feel for the long hours of effort that you and your associates have contributed in the preparation of the excellent report submitted to me has been too long delayed. Your report will be of great value to all who are concerned
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I regard your study as an important document for the consideration of that Commission. In accepting this report ... I want you to know of my genuine gratitude ... Please convey my thanks also to those who assisted you
shared_material.explanation: Both letters combine praise for a submitted study, a statement of its prospective governmental value, and thanks extending to the recipient’s associates.

shared_material.child_excerpt: It will be of immeasurable assistance to the Office of Defense Mobilization, in its preparation of plans for presentation to the National Security Council
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I plan to transmit for study a copy of this report to the head of each department and agency of the Executive Branch concerned with foreign economic policy ... for the consideration of that Commission
shared_material.explanation: Each specifies an administrative route through which the report will inform further executive deliberation.
